requirements.evidence: CreateQueue trims the name, slugifies a default or explicit slug, validates 'max:255', pre-checks the slug per entity and maps a QueryException to a ValidationException (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:17-48). UpdateQueue has nullable named params, excludes the queue itself in slugExists ('id', '!=', $queue->id) and has no delete action (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:15-67,70-77). SetQueueAccess authorizes, checks the entity matches, validates list/string/enum, upserts or deletes, and logs a revoke only when $deleted > 0 (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:22-50). The migration matches the spec, including the unique (entity_membership_id, queue_id) and cascades (migration:14-22). QueuePolicy::call handles managers, the per-queue grant and corrupted values via is_array + array_is_list (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:41-64). CallNextTicket authorizes after the active check (CallNextTicket.php:32). Ticket::call orders the steps lock -> inactive -> authorize -> LogicException (app/Models/Ticket.php:95-105). The enum has one case and the model and factory exist.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through app/Actions and authorize inside via Gate::forUser()->authorize. The policy is auto-discovered in app/Policies. The model uses #[Fillable([...])] like its siblings. The migration has a generated-style timestamp and a reversible down(). docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and the CHANGELOG 'Added' entry are updated. Deviation: unique-violation detection is hand-rolled (SQLSTATE '23000' plus message sniffing) and copy-pasted in two actions instead of using the framework's existing unique-constraint exception.

security.evidence: Every action authorizes first, before any validation or write (CreateQueue.php:18, UpdateQueue.php:22, SetQueueAccess.php:22). Cross-entity membership is rejected (SetQueueAccess.php:24-28). Both call paths enforce 'call' (CallNextTicket.php:32, Ticket.php:101). The old membership-only check is replaced by the stricter policy. Permissions are validated against the enum, and $fillable is set explicitly. No weaknesses found.

tests.evidence: New Pest files cover create, update, set-access, policy and schema/factory. They include unauthorized actors (employee, other entity, non-member, self-grant) with 'writes nothing' assertions, the DB race -> ValidationException case (CreateQueueTest 'turns a database unique collision'), the audit log with mocked context, no log on an empty revoke, corrupted JSON permissions, and every call mode denied (CallNextTicketTest.php:256-273). Ticket::call ordering is tested (IssueTicketTest.php:181-233). Existing tests were updated to use authorized callers, not weakened. Small gap: no race or duplicate-index test for UpdateQueue.

simplicity.evidence: QueueAccessFactory is 117 lines. It overrides Factory::for(), uses cross-referencing closures with a shared &$entity, and has after-making 'align' hooks that forceFill another record's entity_id (database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:59-115). slugExists, duplicateSlug and isUniqueViolation are duplicated almost verbatim between CreateQueue.php:51-76 and UpdateQueue.php:70-97.

readability.evidence: The actions and policy are short, well named, and follow the Gate::forUser style of the sibling actions. The Ticket::call PHPDoc is updated. The factory's resolver and override logic is hard to follow. SetQueueAccessTest has a stray in-test sanity assertion inside the 'forbids non-managers' dataset test (SetQueueAccessTest.php:150-153).

scope.evidence: Every change serves the task: the actions, enum, model, factory, migration, policy, the two call paths, docs and changelog. Edits to existing tests only switch callers to authorized managers, which the new authorization requires. The tests/Pest.php helper queueManagerFor supports the new tests. No UI and no delete action were added.

issues.explanation: Overriding Factory::for() and silently forceFill-ing the entity_id of an existing membership or queue to make them match is over-engineered, and it can hide test bugs by moving records between entities instead of failing.
slugExists, duplicateSlug and isUniqueViolation are copy-pasted between the two actions.

isUniqueViolation treats any SQLSTATE 23000 (which also covers FK and NOT NULL violations) as a duplicate slug and relies on message sniffing, instead of catching Laravel's existing unique-constraint exception.
No test covers the UpdateQueue path where the DB unique index (race) is turned into a ValidationException, or an overly long updated name.
A fixture sanity assertion is mixed into the authorization test body; it adds noise without testing behavior.

review.summary: The change adds CreateQueue, UpdateQueue and SetQueueAccess actions, the queue_access table, model, factory and enum, and a QueuePolicy enforced by both CallNextTicket and Ticket::call(), with docs and thorough Pest tests. Requirements, authorization and test coverage are solid. Points come off for an over-engineered QueueAccess factory that rewrites related records' entities, and for slug and unique-violation helpers duplicated across two actions. I would approve after these nits are addressed.
